title: Supply an application-specific cross-origin verdict
goal: Define an explicit set of trusted browser origins when application write policy must differ from automatic Fetch Metadata and credentialed CORS trust.

selectionNotes: Custom DI service with operator-owned exact origins; rejects missing Origin. Real Minimal API form consumption, distinct from token-required and JSON paths.

packageAssets: Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web implicit Microsoft.AspNetCore.App reference; these non-Razor consumers restore no NuGet libraries. Internal.Assets is not the ICsrfProtection contract or a required direct package here.
providers: ExchangeProtection registered as singleton ICsrfProtection; exact ExchangeOrigins from operator-owned appsettings.json; built-in provider in --standard true comparison; built-in antiforgery with ephemeral Data Protection in separate --tokens true mode
platforms: ASP.NET Core server; measured Windows x64 Chrome156 with disposable HTTP loopback hosts; production requires HTTPS and independently secured trusted origins
renderingModes: Ordinary HTML forms and browser fetch to Minimal API form binding; no Blazor or MVC rendering claim
prerequisites: Copy the complete standalone SeedExchange files. Empty Directory files isolate inherited build/package configuration. Configure exact trusted serialized origins at deployment; validate ownership of every trusted site. UseAntiforgery is retained only in separate token-required mode.
constraints: The custom rule accepts safe methods and exact configured Origin only. It does not infer trust from same-site, Sec-Fetch-Site, Host, wildcard CORS or read permission. Missing/null/multiple/unlisted origins are denied for protected writes; token-required clients need the separate token mode or their own endpoint design.

Automatic RC2 middleware obtains ICsrfProtection from DI, records a verdict and relies on form-binding consumers with RequiresValidation metadata to reject before the handler. JSON lacks that metadata and stays unchanged. Arbitrary endpoints/metadata alone are not proof of enforcement.

The standard provider accepts same-origin Fetch Metadata and headerless non-browser requests. Other browser origins need explicit credentialed CORS trust. This custom provider deliberately decouples write trust from CORS: a trusted form may execute even when the browser cannot read its response.

Retain token pairs for token-dependent browsers, compliance or additional-data requirements. The --tokens true comparison uses the standard provider and token middleware; RC2 token middleware can overwrite its automatic verdict. It is not a composed custom-origin-plus-token policy. The .NET10 comparison explicitly enforces both origin and tokens.

The sample has no authentication, authorization or persistence. Integrate the real application identity/permission checks independently. Browser-controlled headers are not credentials; non-browser clients can forge them. This is not an authorization mechanism, XSS defense or universal CSRF proof. Test proxy/HTTPS/origin configuration separately.

The /observations, /session and /controls.html diagnostics are disposable local proof only. Do not expose them publicly. No user key store, public publication, provider account, native package or optional workload is used.
optIns: Explicit AddSingleton<ICsrfProtection, ExchangeProtection> replaces automatic policy globally for protected endpoints; keep the override small and deliberate.
stabilityLimitations: No ExperimentalAttribute on these actual public contracts. Stable API designation with RC2-specific artifacts and observed behavior; actual GA, other browsers/OSs, proxy, MVC/Razor Pages/SSR and deployment behavior remain unqualified. PIN-959/PIN-964 remain open.
